edges.mechanism: Ascorbate reduces/chelates non-heme iron, increasing absorption
edges.evidence: Stable-isotope study (80 mg AA +30% fractional absorption; 500 mg no further gain) and balance RCT; moderate

edges.mechanism: Enhanced non-heme iron absorption may exacerbate iron overload
edges.evidence: Official fact sheet statement (mechanistic/clinical consensus); low

edges.mechanism: Pro-oxidant high-dose (esp. IV) ascorbate causes oxidative hemolysis in G6PD-deficient red cells
edges.evidence: Case meta-summary (14 cases, 71% G6PD-deficient), IV label warning, scoping review; low but serious

edges.mechanism: Ascorbate metabolised to oxalate; risk of oxalate nephropathy
edges.evidence: Biopsy series (supplement-associated oxalate nephropathy rose to 44% of cases; 49% had CKD), IV label warning; low

edges.mechanism: Increased urinary oxalate; supplemental >=1 g/day associated with stones in men
edges.evidence: Prospective cohorts (men HR 1.19 for supplemental >=1 g/day; total >=1 g/day HR 1.43) and MA; no association in women; low-moderate

edges.mechanism: Antioxidant cocktail (incl. vitamin C) blunted HDL2 rise and angiographic benefit of simvastatin-niacin
edges.evidence: HATS RCT (n=160) and lipoprotein sub-study; antioxidant mixture not vitamin C alone; low-moderate

edges.mechanism: Antioxidants attenuated HDL2/Lp(A-I) response to niacin+simvastatin
Antioxidants might protect tumour cells from oxidative chemotherapy/radiation (contested); IV ascorbate also studied as an intended adjunct
edges.evidence: Official fact sheet notes controversy; phase II RCTs mixed (pancreatic OS benefit, prostate futility); low

edges.mechanism: Ascorbic acid inactivates bleomycin in vitro
edges.evidence: FDA IV ascorbic acid label (in vitro); very low
Case reports of warfarin resistance reversing on stopping AA; label notes no effect at <=1 g/day for 2 weeks; very low

edges.mechanism: Urinary acidification increases renal excretion, lowering serum levels (also fluphenazine)
Co-administration abolished endothelial-function benefit seen with either vitamin alone
Ascorbate (reducing agent) interferes with redox/electrochemical glucose assays; high IV doses falsely elevate point-of-care readings; urine dipstick glucose false negatives
edges.evidence: Case series (POC overestimation 10-200 mg/dL during IV infusion), meter comparison, FDA label, dipstick study; moderate

edges.with: urine dipstick (hemoglobin, nitrite, bilirubin, leukocyte esterase)
edges.mechanism: Reducing agent inhibits peroxidase/diazo reactions, causing false negatives
edges.evidence: Laboratory interference study; FDA label; moderate

edges.mechanism: Inhibits pseudoperoxidase reaction of heme causing false-negative results
edges.evidence: Case/in vitro study and systematic review recommending withholding before gFOBT; low

edges.mechanism: IV high-dose vitamin C in vasopressor-dependent sepsis increased death/persistent organ dysfunction
edges.evidence: LOVIT RCT (RR 1.21) plus null C-EASIE RCT and umbrella review not supporting routine use; moderate

edges.mechanism: SVCT1 transporter variant lowers circulating ascorbate (~6 umol/L per allele)
edges.evidence: Genetic association meta-analysis >15,000 participants; no dosing evidence; low
